questions.stem: According to the passage, when did the U.S. Supreme Court rule that college athletes could earn money from their name, image and likeness?
questions.evidence: that changed in 2021 when the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that athletes could earn money by selling their name, image and likeness
questions.explanation_ko: 2021년 미국 대법원이 선수들이 이름·이미지·초상권을 판매해 돈을 벌 수 있다고 판결했다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT given as a reason an athlete mentioned for staying in or transferring within college sports?
options: Earning NIL money at another school
Meeting a required minimum GPA of 4.0
questions.evidence: Now, the top athletes can enter what is called a transfer portal to get more NIL money at another school and compete right away.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from Bottorff's comment that things "haven't really changed that much" and athletes "just got an extra little bit of cash"?
options: NIL deals have made every college athlete wealthy.
For most college athletes, NIL has brought only a small amount of extra money compared to star athletes.
NIL money is no longer allowed for any college athlete.
Only football players are eligible for NIL deals.
questions.evidence: We just got an extra little bit of cash in our pockets
questions.explanation_ko: 대부분의 선수에게는 큰 변화가 없었고 약간의 돈만 더 생겼다는 말에서, 유명 선수들과 달리 NIL의 재정적 영향이 크지 않았음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author include the story of Tavarius Covington, who hopes to be the first in his family to attend college?
options: To illustrate that, for many younger athletes, earning a college degree is still the main dream, not NIL money
To criticize young athletes who want to play sports
To explain a rule change in college transfers
To promote a specific college's football program
questions.evidence: A college education remains a dream for many younger athletes.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 사례는 많은 젊은 선수들에게 여전히 대학 학위 취득이 가장 중요한 꿈임을 보여 주기 위해 소개되었습니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "scholarship" mean in "transferred to Northern Arizona University on a football scholarship"?
options: money or support given to help pay for education
questions.evidence: transferred to Northern Arizona University on a football scholarship
questions.explanation_ko: scholarship은 교육비를 지원하기 위해 주어지는 돈이나 지원을 뜻합니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 하지만 여러 선수는 AP에 NIL을 통해 얻는 돈은 학위를 따고 좋아하는 운동을 하는 것에 비하면 사소한 고려 사항이라고 말했다.

blanks.meaning: 한 해 경기에 출전하지 않고 쉬다
blanks.sentence_ko: 이전 규정에서는 선수들이 경기에 출전하기 전에 한 해를 쉬어야 했다.
물론 우리가 컨퍼런스 챔피언십에서 두 번 우승하면 상황이 달라지긴 하죠.
저는 동생에게 고등학교를 졸업하고 나면 더 기대할 만한 것들이 있다는 걸 알려 주고 싶어요, 라고 Covington은 말했다.

key_points: Since a 2021 Supreme Court ruling allowed college athletes to earn money from their name, image, and likeness (NIL), some famous athletes have made large sums, but most athletes say a college degree still matters more.
Several athletes interviewed said NIL money has changed little for most players and is not their main reason for staying in or transferring between schools.
New transfer rules let top athletes move to another school and compete immediately in pursuit of better NIL deals, though some payment disputes have occurred.
For many athletes, including younger ones still in high school, earning a college degree remains the biggest goal of playing college sports.
main_idea: While a 2021 Supreme Court ruling now allows college athletes to earn NIL money, most athletes interviewed say that earning a college degree remains their main goal, more important than the money.
restate_sentence: But several athletes told The Associated Press that the money available to them through NIL remains a small consideration compared with earning a degree and competing in the sports they love.
